Mattan
MAT-tan
n. (proper, a priest of Baal; Hebrew, a gift)
Hebrew Mattan, a gift — from nathan, to give. The irony is unmissable: the priest of Baal slain before his own altars bore a name meaning gift, and Scripture names a second Mattan, father of one of Jeremiah's persecutors.

Biblical Definition

When Jehoiada the priest brought the boy Joash out of hiding and crowned him, the covenant renewal did not stop at the palace: “And all the people of the land went into the house of Baal, and brake it down; his altars and his images brake they in pieces thoroughly, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars” (2 Kings 11:18). The chronicler records the same act in the same terms (2 Chronicles 23:17). Athaliah's six-year reign had installed a rival worship with its own house, its own images and its own priesthood, and a reformation that had left the house of Baal standing would have been no reformation. A second Mattan appears in Jeremiah's day as the father of Shephatiah, one of the princes who heard Jeremiah's words and demanded his death (Jeremiah 38:1) — the men who then put the prophet in the miry dungeon.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as the name of the priest of Baal slain before the altars in the reformation under Jehoiada.

expand to see more

BAAL, n. The chief male deity of the Phoenicians and Canaanites; a name signifying lord or master.

REFORMATION, n. Change from worse to better; amendment of life; the great religious revolution of the sixteenth century.

IMAGE, n. A representation or similitude of any person or thing, formed of a material substance; an idol.

COVENANT, n. A mutual consent or agreement of two or more persons; in Scripture, God's gracious engagement with his people.

IDOLATRY, n. The worship of idols, images, or any thing made by hands, or which is not God.

Key Scripture

2 Kings 11:18 — "And all the people of the land went into the house of Baal, and brake it down; his altars and his images brake they in pieces thoroughly, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. And the priest appointed officers over the house of the LORD."

2 Chronicles 23:17 — "Then all the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down, and brake his altars and his images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars."

Jeremiah 38:1 — "Then Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashur, and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchiah, heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken unto all the people, saying,"

2 Kings 11:17 — "And Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they should be the LORD'S people; between the king also and the people."

Modern Corruption

Reformation is imagined as a change of personal conviction that leaves rival institutions standing; under Jehoiada the covenant was renewed and the house of Baal was broken down the same day.

expand to see more

The reformation under Jehoiada has a shape that later reformers recognized. First a covenant — between the LORD and the king and the people, that they should be the LORD'S people — and then, immediately, the house of Baal broken down, the altars and images broken thoroughly, and the priest of Baal slain before the altars. Nothing was left standing to be returned to. A repentance that renews vows while carefully preserving the machinery of the old idolatry has not repented; Scripture's pattern is that the high places come down, and Judah's kings are judged, one after another, by whether they did.

Two cautions belong here. The first is that the civil sword used in 2 Kings 11 was Israel's under a theocratic covenant, not the church's in this age; our weapons are not carnal, and idols today are broken by preaching, discipline and repentance rather than by execution. The second is the name. Mattan means gift, and the second Mattan in Scripture fathered a man who sought a prophet's life. A good name, a respectable office and a religious vocabulary are no evidence at all of which side of a reformation a man will be found on.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Mattan (H4977), a gift; nathan (H5414), to give; Baal (H1168), lord; mizbeach (H4196), an altar.

expand to see more

Hebrew Mattan (H4977) — a gift; the name of the priest of Baal slain before the altars.

Hebrew nathan (H5414) — to give; the root of Mattan, Nathan, Mattaniah and Jonathan.

Hebrew Baal (H1168) — lord, master; the Canaanite deity Athaliah had established in Judah.

Hebrew mizbeach (H4196) — an altar, a place of slaughter; where his own end came.

Hebrew beriyth (H1285) — a covenant; renewed by Jehoiada before the house of Baal fell.

Usage

"“Slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars” — nothing left standing."

"“Brake his altars and his images in pieces” — thoroughly, says the text."

"“Shephatiah the son of Mattan” — a good name on a bad side."
